title: Corporate Credit Risk Agents
description: A code-driven orchestrator coordinates six specialist agents (financial, sector, prior reports, charts, report writer and validator) to produce a corporate-banking credit report, exportable to Word and PowerPoint.
problem: A corporate credit report combines financial statements, sector context and the history of prior reports, and then has to be written up and presented to a committee. The system splits that work across specialist agents and delivers a validated, export-ready report that the analyst reviews instead of building from scratch.

architecture.caption: Five layers: analyst and application, code-driven orchestration, specialist agents, tools and knowledge via MCP, and data.

nodes.name: Corporate banking analyst
nodes.detail: Requests, reviews and exports the report

nodes.name: Code-driven orchestrator
nodes.detail: Sets the order and consolidates results

flow: The analyst starts the evaluation of a corporate client. The code-driven orchestrator decides which agents take part and in what order.
Document Intelligence extracts the financial statements and the financial agent computes ratios and trends.
The sector agent adds market context and the prior-reports agent retrieves previous evaluations from Azure AI Search.
The charts agent generates the visuals that accompany the analysis.
The report writer consolidates everything into the credit report and the validator agent checks its consistency before delivery.
The report is exported to Word and PowerPoint for review and committee presentation.

components.name: Microsoft Foundry
components.role: Models and agents of the system.

components.name: Agent Framework
components.role: Code-driven orchestration of the six agents.

components.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
components.role: Standard contract between agents and tools.

insight.title: Orchestrated by code, not by prompt
insight.text: The agent order is decided by code, not by the model. That makes the process predictable and auditable, and allows a validator agent at the end of the chain: no report reaches the analyst without a consistency check.
